target: credibility gates (METHODS_COMPARISON.md:50-56, VERIFICATION.md): what a GPU solver can pass while still being wrong for the cage slip-out problem
claim: The five gates are code-to-code checks against FEBio on the same input decks, plus one trivially uniform friction test. A GPU solver can pass all of them and still give a wrong slip-out answer. Six gaps: (1) Errors in the input deck (load curves, boundary conditions, surface pairing) are reproduced identically by both codes; I-001 is exactly this case and would have passed gates 2 and 3. (2) Gate 1c is close to tautological: the slip traction is mu * p_n by construction (contact.py:164), and the pass criterion is |F_t / F_n - mu| < 2 %. (3) Not tested at all: stick memory over increments (F-0003), friction under spin, load reversal and cycling, curved or tilted faces, and the voxel staircase against a tet-mesh endplate. The GPU code also uses slave nodes, whereas FEBio uses facet integration points. (4) The one place where GPU and FEBio friction differ, about 8 %, is attributed to FEBio without evidence: at mu 0.5 GPU slides at 0.496 and FEBio at 0.457, and at the onset t 0.525 the values are 0.279 vs 0.256. Yet FEBio (L2) supplies 'the only numbers reported as results' (PLAN.md:47). (5) Gate 3 uses one design (p062, regular window cage, tied contact, so no friction). Free-form voxel designs are not covered: 2-voxel struts, soft phi 0 contact faces, many cavities. (6) Nothing checks the 1 mm translation criterion's sensitivity to penalty and increment size. Elastic micro-slip from the penalty counts toward the cage translation.
evidence: METHODS_COMPARISON.md:51-55 (gate list); VERIFICATION.md:12 (1c result and the FEBio 0.457 remark); gate1c_report.json mu 0.5 rows t 0.525 (gpu_ratio 0.2786, febio_ratio 0.2561, both 'stick_frac' 1.0 on GPU) and t 1.0 (0.4962 vs 0.4569); contact.py:164 'fslip = pn * nrm + mu * pn * tdir'; gate1c_friction.py:75 pass rule 'err < 0.02'; F-0001 for a deck bug that both codes share; contact.py:7-9 node-to-facet vs FESlidingElasticInterface integration-point data (FESlidingElasticInterface.cpp:775 'GetMaterialPoint(n)' of surface element). Validation against physical experiments (ASME V&V 40-2018 'validation' step; e.g. cage push-out / expulsion tests) is not planned anywhere in PLAN.md or METHODS_COMPARISON.md.
how_to_reproduce: Read the cited lines; compare gate1c_report.json rows at t 0.525 and 1.0 for mu 0.5.

fix_options.option: Add deck-level checks independent of both solvers (F-0001 option 2) and make them part of every gate

Add friction benchmarks with known answers: (a) a rigid disc under torque (spin starts at T = 2/3 mu N R for uniform pressure - Goyal, Ruina & Papadopoulos 1991, Wear 143:307), (b) combined shear + torque against the limit surface, (c) stick-hold-reverse cycles (F-0003), (d) a tilted / curved interface, (e) the voxel staircase cage face on a real endplate patch vs FEBio, (f) penalty and increment halving on the cage translation

Explain the 8 % GPU-FEBio friction gap before gate 4 (e.g. FEBio augmentation / gap tolerance settings, integration-point vs node discretisation); if it cannot be explained, carry it as a stated L1-L2 bias
Plan at least one physical validation point for slip-out (literature cage expulsion / push-out data, or a bench test) per ASME V&V 40

summary_zh: 目前的五道驗證關卡，基本上都是「同一份輸入檔交給 GPU 和 FEBio 各算一次，比較兩者是否一致」，外加一個非常簡單的摩擦滑塊測試。因此，GPU 求解器可以全部通過，對 cage 滑出問題卻仍然算錯。缺口有六：（1）輸入檔本身寫錯時，兩個程式會一起錯，I-001 就是這種情況；（2）摩擦滑塊測試幾乎是循環論證，因為程式本來就直接寫著「滑動摩擦力等於摩擦係數乘以正壓力」；（3）沒有測試黏著記憶、扭轉摩擦、來回反向與循環負荷、斜面或曲面，也沒有測試階梯狀的體素表面；（4）GPU 與 FEBio 在摩擦上相差約 8%，文件直接歸咎於 FEBio，但沒有證據，而最後對外報告的數字正是來自 FEBio；（5）cage 驗證只用了一個傳統設計，而且是黏住、沒有摩擦的情況；（6）也沒有檢查「1 毫米滑移」這個判斷標準，會不會受接觸剛度與步長影響。此外，計畫中完全沒有用實體實驗來驗證。
